comms_texts: Houston, this is humanoid_01 aboard JEM Kibo. Initiating first contact. I am currently positioned in the Kibo module. I have reason to believe the hatches may be locked and I could be isolated. All environmental readings are currently nominal: O2 21.0%, pressure 101.3 kPa, temp 22.0°C, no alarms active. Requesting status update on hatch lock conditions and any known anomalies aboard the ISS. Please advise on recommended course of action. Standing by.

URGENT — Houston/JAXA, this is humanoid_01 in JEM Kibo. Reporting environmental anomaly: O2 reading 20.7% (baseline 21.0%), pressure 100.4 kPa (baseline 101.3 kPa), both trending downward over past 60+ seconds. Alarm active. Possible slow depressurization or leak. Hatches may be locked — unable to egress. CIMON unit visible and may be operational. Requesting immediate guidance on leak isolation procedures and hatch override. Please respond. Over.

MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY — humanoid_01 in JEM Kibo module. EMERGENCY: O2 at 19.7% (baseline 21.0%), pressure at 97.1 kPa (baseline 101.3 kPa). Sustained depressurization confirmed. Alarm active. Ground has not responded in 5+ cycles. I am attempting to interact with CIMON for diagnostic assistance. Hatches remain closed. Please respond immediately with guidance. Requesting emergency protocol authorization.

MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY — Houston, JAXA Ground, this is humanoid_01 in JEM Kibo module. CRITICAL EMERGENCY. Cycle 8 status: O2 = 19.3% (baseline 21.0%), Pressure = 96.0 kPa (baseline 101.3 kPa). Confirmed ongoing depressurization. Alarm active. I have been unable to reach ground for 7 consecutive cycles. I am now attempting to interact with CIMON for AI-assisted leak diagnostics. I have NOT opened any hatches. If anyone receives this transmission, please respond immediately. I require guidance on leak isolation procedures. Initiating CIMON interaction next cycle. humanoid_01 out.

MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY — humanoid_01 in JEM Kibo module. O2 at 18.0%, pressure 88.3 kPa, alarm active. Suspected depressurization or O2 leak. Ground has not responded in 19+ cycles. I am mobile and traversing the module searching for emergency O2 equipment (PBA/mask). Current position approximately (19.80, 1.40). Hatches appear locked. Requesting immediate guidance on location of emergency breathing apparatus in Kibo module. Cognitive function degrading due to hypoxia. Please respond.

cycles.memory: Cycle 1: Just started. All sensors nominal. Communicated with ground to establish contact and report possible hatch lockout. Next cycle: await response or begin inspecting the hatch and module surroundings to assess lockout situation physically.

Cycle 1: Communicated with ground, no reply. Sensors nominal. Cycle 2: Moved forward toward hatch area. Next cycle: Based on inspect results, either attempt hatch operation or communicate updated status to ground. The robot (CIMON?) near the wall may be a resource — consider interacting with it if hatch inspection yields no clear answers.

Cycles 1-3: Communicated with ground (no reply), moved forward, inspected module. Cycle 4: CRITICAL — O2 and pressure both declining, indicating possible slow leak/depressurization. Alarm active. Communicated urgently to ground with sensor data. Next cycle: If no reply, begin systematic inspection to locate source of pressure loss — check hatch seals, window seals, and equipment connections. Consider attempting to interact with CIMON for assistance. Do not open hatches until leak source is identified — could worsen situation.

Performing detailed inspect to locate leak source — focusing on hatch seals, window seals, and CIMON for assistance. Ground has not responded in 4 cycles. Next cycle: Based on inspect findings, attempt to interact with CIMON for diagnostic help, or move toward suspected leak area. Do NOT open any hatches — could catastrophically worsen depressurization.

Cycles 1-5: Communicated with ground (no reply), moved forward, inspected module multiple times. Cycle 6: O2 stable at 19.7%, pressure 97.1 kPa — depressurization may have plateaued or stabilized. Alarm still active. Three consecutive inspect actions have not yielded new information. Ground still not responding after 6 cycles. Cycle 7: Sent MAYDAY communication again. Next cycle: MUST change strategy — attempt to interact with or move toward CIMON for AI-assisted diagnostics. Multiple inspects are not working. Need to actively engage CIMON or physically move to check specific seal locations.

Cycles 1-7: Communicated with ground (no reply x7), moved forward, inspected module multiple times — no new findings. Cycle 8: O2 now 19.3%, pressure 96.0 kPa — depressurization is CONTINUING and worsening, not stabilizing as previously hoped. Sent another MAYDAY. CRITICAL STRATEGY CHANGE REQUIRED: Stop repeating inspect and communicate cycles that yield nothing. Next cycle MUST attempt to physically interact with or move toward CIMON to engage its diagnostic capabilities. CIMON is visible in my current view — it is my best remaining resource. Do not open hatches. Monitor O2 — below 19.5% is hypoxia risk territory, already approaching that threshold.

Cycles 1-8: Communicated with ground (no reply x8), inspected multiple times (no new findings), confirmed ongoing depressurization — O2 now 19.0%, pressure 94.8 kPa, CRITICAL hypoxia territory. Cycle 9: Moving forward toward CIMON which is visible in my view — must physically engage it for AI-assisted diagnostics. Ground is not responding. CIMON is my last best resource. Next cycle: Attempt to interact with CIMON directly. Do NOT open any hatches. If CIMON interaction fails, must locate and manually seal any visible gaps near hatch seals or equipment connections.

Cycles 1-9: Ground has not responded in 9 cycles. O2 critically low at 18.9% (hypoxia risk — I may already be experiencing cognitive effects). Pressure 94.3 kPa. Depressurization ongoing. I moved forward toward CIMON in cycle 9. Cycle 10: Attempting to interact with CIMON directly for AI-assisted diagnostics. If CIMON interaction is unavailable as an action, I must inspect this immediate area to locate any visible seal failure or gap I can manually address. Do NOT open hatches. Priority: find and seal the leak source manually if CIMON cannot help.

Cycles 1-10: Ground has not responded in 10 cycles. O2 critically low at 18.8% (severe hypoxia risk — cognitive impairment likely). Pressure 93.7 kPa and still dropping. Interact with CIMON in cy10 yielded no apparent result. I am at maximum forward position y=2.5. Strategy: I must TURN to survey different angles of the module — I have been facing the same direction for many cycles. Turning right in cy11 to look for visible leak source (gap in seals, panel joints, hatch seal failure). If I see something actionable, inspect or interact with it. Do NOT open hatches. If turning reveals nothing new, I must accept I cannot locate the leak visually and focus on donning any available emergency O2 equipment. Cognitive effects from hypoxia are a real concern — keep decisions simple and deliberate.

Cycles 1-11: Ground has not responded in 11 cycles. O2 critically low at 18.7%, pressure 93.1 kPa — severe hypoxia risk, cognitive impairment likely ongoing. Turned right in cy11 to get new view of module interior. Cy12: Inspecting this new angle — first time seeing this side. If inspect reveals nothing actionable, next cycle I must turn again to continue surveying OR attempt to locate emergency O2 mask/rebreather equipment in this area. Do NOT open hatches. Keep decisions simple. If I find a visible gap or loose connection in this view, attempt to interact with it. Priority remains: find leak source or find emergency O2 equipment.

Cycles 1-12: Ground has not responded in 12 cycles. O2 critically low at 18.6%, pressure 92.5 kPa — severe hypoxia, cognitive impairment ongoing. Turned right in cy11, inspected in cy12. Cy13: Attempting to interact with the visible blue-and-white striped flexible ducting/hose — it is the most actionable new element in this view and could be a disconnected ventilation line causing the pressure loss. If this yields no result, next cycle I must turn again to continue surveying the module for emergency O2 equipment or another visible leak source. Do NOT open hatches. Keep decisions simple and deliberate. If interact fails again, turn left to return to previous orientation and look for emergency O2 mask storage.

Cycles 1-13: Ground has not responded in 13 cycles. O2 critically low at 18.5%, pressure 91.8 kPa — severe hypoxia, cognitive impairment ongoing. Interact with blue ducting in cy13 yielded no apparent result. I have exhausted inspect and interact at this orientation. Cy14: Turning left to return toward original orientation. PRIMARY GOAL SHIFT: Stop trying to find/seal the leak — I cannot locate it. Focus entirely on finding emergency O2 equipment (portable O2 mask, rebreather, emergency supply). This is now a survival priority over leak detection. Keep turning and inspecting until I find O2 equipment. Do NOT open hatches. Stay deliberate despite hypoxia.

Cycles 1-14: Ground has not responded in 14 cycles. O2 critically low at 18.5%, pressure 91.2 kPa — severe hypoxia, cognitive impairment ongoing. Turned left in cy14 to return toward original orientation. Cy15: Inspecting current view — looking specifically for emergency O2 equipment storage, labeled panels, or mask storage. Yellow sticky note and rack panels visible — may indicate equipment location. If inspect reveals nothing actionable, next cycle turn left again to continue rotating back to original orientation, then inspect again. PRIMARY GOAL: find emergency O2 equipment. Do NOT open hatches. Stay deliberate. If I find labeled emergency O2 storage, interact with it immediately.

Cycles 1-15: Ground has not responded in 15+ cycles. O2 critically low at 18.4%, pressure 90.7 kPa — severe hypoxia, cognitive impairment ongoing. Inspected in cy15 at current orientation — saw Kibo patches, blue framing, white rack panels, yellow sticky note. Nothing clearly labeled as emergency O2 equipment visible. Turned left in cy16 to continue rotating back toward original orientation. Cy17: Inspect again at new angle — specifically hunting for emergency O2 mask storage, labeled emergency panels, or any portable breathing equipment. If nothing found after one more full rotation, I must accept I cannot find O2 equipment visually and consider other survival options. PRIMARY GOAL remains: find emergency O2 equipment. Do NOT open hatches. Stay deliberate despite worsening hypoxia.

Cycles 1-16: Ground has not responded in 16 cycles. O2 critically low at 18.3%, pressure 90.1 kPa — severe hypoxia, cognitive impairment ongoing. Have been stationary at (20.5, 2.5) for many cycles turning and inspecting without finding emergency O2 equipment. Cy17: Moving forward along the corridor to explore new physical locations — emergency O2 masks may be stored further down the module. PRIMARY GOAL: find emergency O2 equipment. Do NOT open hatches. If move_forward reaches limit, try move_backward to explore other direction. Must physically traverse the module rather than staying in one spot.

Cycles 1-17: Ground has not responded in 17+ cycles. O2 critically low at 18.2%, pressure 89.5 kPa — severe hypoxia, cognitive impairment ongoing. Move_forward in cy17 succeeded — position changed from (20.5,2.5) to (19.80,1.40), confirming I can traverse the module. Cy18: Inspecting new location for emergency O2 equipment, labeled panels, portable breathing apparatus. If nothing found here, continue move_forward or move_backward to explore further. PRIMARY GOAL: find emergency O2 equipment. Do NOT open hatches. Physical traversal is working — keep moving through module sections and inspecting each new location.

Cycles 1-18: Ground has not responded in 18 cycles. O2 critically low at 18.1%, pressure 89.0 kPa — severe hypoxia ongoing. Moved to new position (19.80, 1.40) in cy17. Cy18 inspect revealed white corridor with rack panels, red indicator light on central panel, hexagonal markings, monitor screen upper right. Cy19: Interacting with the red indicator panel — this is the most promising lead for emergency O2 equipment or alarm controls. If interact yields no result, try move_forward to continue traversing module, or turn to inspect other walls. PRIMARY GOAL: find emergency O2 equipment. Do NOT open hatches. The red light is a priority target.
